doc.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Sweets Edison's sayings and playing today
summary: Capp shares Sweets Edison's colorful colloquialisms and says Sweets still has great time but now sits to play.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well we spoke with them yesterday and it was marvelous.

Oh you talked with them? That must have been great. I mean Sweets has got some of the funniest expressions — I doubt whether he used them all — but you know like some of those Southern colloquialisms you call them. Like, “He’s tighter than a chicken’s instep.” You know that kind of thing. Or, “He’s so cheap he’s got enough money to air condition a cotton field.
One of the guys said, “If he looked any sharper I’d be bleeding.”

He’s got a million of those, and some that I wouldn’t want to talk about here. But Sweets is great. And it was so much fun playing with him. He still has that great sense of time and swing. He doesn’t have to play a lot of notes. And tempo doesn’t bother him, anything. The only thing I noticed last night, which I haven’t worked with Sweets now for a couple of years. I haven’t been on the same stand with him. But I noticed he has to sit down now when he plays — he sits on a chair. I did a tour with Sweets and Buck
